newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, Japan to hold talks on disputed isles next week.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, Japan to hold talks on disputed isles next week.

text.p: Taiwan will hold talks with Japan on fishery disputes over a chain of East China Sea islands next week, foreign minister John Chang said on Saturday.
"The second round of talks will be held in early October, on either October 3 or October 4, in Japan. I can confirm that," Chang told journalists, broadcast on state-funded television.
The last fishery talks were held in early August in Taipei.
"As for the level and content of the talks, we need further discussions," Chang said.
Asked whether the two sides would discuss sovereignty issues during the meeting in Japan, Chang said: "All kinds of issues will be touched."

Tensions have run high in the East China Sea since July when a Japanese right-wing group built a lighthouse and planted flags on the uninhabited islands, known by the Chinese as the Diaoyus and the Japanese as the Senkakus.

On Thursday, a voyage to the islands by a Hong Kong protest group ended in tragedy when its leader, David Chan, drowned after he and four other protesters jumped into the storm-whipped sea to defy Japan's claims.
The islands -- west of Japan's Okinawa island, northeast of Taiwan and east of China's southeastern Fujian coast -- are claimed by Taiwan, China and Japan.
Taiwanese fishermen have complained that Japan's patrol boats barred them from catching fish near the islands, endangering their livelihood.
The cluster of uninhabited rocky outcrops in the East China Sea has kindled fiery passions among Chinese communities in Hong Kong, China, Taiwan and Macau.
Japan has claimed sovereign rights to the islands and refused to acknowledge that the dispute is still open for discussion with China.
Tokyo's claim dates to 1895, when Japan defeated China and seized Taiwan and other territories. China has claimed sovereignty over the islands for centuries.
